title: Mario finds his right B-52 pilot glove missing from his bag
place_text: Ellsworth AFB / Mario's home, Rapid City, South Dakota

tellings.quote: I did everything. And my left hand glove was there, but the right hand glove is gone.

I had not even thought about the mittens after that night—those heavy Air Force-issue gloves with open fingers, so you could fire a weapon—but, when he said that, I ran to my ditty bag to check and they were not there.

plain: After his strange night at a South Dakota missile site in 1977, the Air Force guard Mario Woods says he went to his bag at home in Rapid City and found one of his gloves gone. He tells Michels he checked everything: "my left hand glove was there, but the right hand glove is gone," and he describes them as B-52 pilot gloves. He mentions a man named Michael Johnson as part of this telling. Woods had written about the gloves earlier for the journalist Robert Hastings, whose article on the case was published on 10 September 2017. That version is a little different. Woods writes that he had not thought about "those heavy Air Force-issue gloves with open fingers, so you could fire a weapon" until someone brought them up, and that when he ran to his ditty bag "they were not there", meaning both of them. The two tellings disagree on what kind of gloves they were and on whether one or both went missing. Woods brings it up because a missing glove would be a physical trace of a night he can hardly remember.

discussion.by: Former USAF Missile Security Policeman Tells of Apparent UFO Abduction at ICBM Site
discussion.text: In the account Woods wrote for Hastings in 2017 both of his "mittens", "those heavy Air Force-issue gloves with open fingers, so you could fire a weapon", "were not there" in his ditty bag; the later telling has the right glove of a pair of B-52 pilot gloves gone and the left one still in the bag. The two tellings differ in which gloves and how many.
